Population increased in Wolverhampton

The estimated population of Wolverhampton in 2024 was 281,251 usual residents, a rise of 2.1% since 2023.

This meant that Wolverhampton's rate of population change placed it among the 10 percent fastest growing local authority districts in England and Wales.

In the period from mid-2021 to mid-2024, the population estimate of Wolverhampton increased by 6.4%.

Over this slightly longer period, Wolverhampton was also among the 10% fastest growing local authority districts in England and Wales.

Age profile of Wolverhampton

The average (median) age fell to 37.4 years between 2023 and 2024.

You can see how the age profile of Wolverhampton has changed since 2011 in the population pyramid below.

sections.content:
Wolverhampton is an area that is classed as urban in nature according to the 2021 Census Rural Urban Classification.

By age category, Wolverhampton's population of 281,251 usual residents was made up of:

  • 60,611 people aged 0 to 15 years, (21.6%)
  • 175,532 people aged 16 to 64 years, (62.4%)
  • 45,108 people aged 65 years and over, (16%)

    • Compared with England and Wales as a whole, Wolverhampton has a slightly higher proportion of people aged 0 to 15 years (21.6% compared with 18.3% for England and Wales).

Contributors to population change

We look at different flows of people into and out of areas and births and deaths to see what is driving population change in each area.

In Wolverhampton, the largest contribution to population change in the year to mid-2024 was from net international migration.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in Wolverhampton
sections.subtitle: How the population changed, by component

sections.content:
We estimate that, for Wolverhampton, between 2023 and 2024:

  • More births than deaths increased the population of 694 people (0.3%). In total, there were 3,450 births and 2,756 deaths in Wolverhampton.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other areas in the UK) led to a fall in the population of 2,282 (-0.8%). There were 13,935 people entering the area and 16,217 people leaving the area.
  • Net international migration led to an increase in Wolverhampton's population of 7,260 (2.6%) as a result of 9,449 people entering the area and 2,189 people leaving the area.
  • Other change (which includes changes to armed forces personnel and prisoners) for Wolverhampton was less than 0.1%.

Revisions to 2023 population estimates

We regularly revise our initial population estimates as we get more data and methods improve.

Our revised estimate for the population of Wolverhampton in mid-2023 is 275,601.

Within this, international migration was revised upwards by 3,227 people and internal migration estimates were revised downwards by 51 people.

Overall, there was an revision upwards of 3,176 people.
